canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Avoid application-wide technical buckets and empty architecture folders; keep feature-specific code within the feature and keep core/shared relatively small.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Feature locality, no same-feature sharing pretext and genuinely cross-feature shared scope explicit.

Empty or speculative folders: `.claude/rules/angular.md`. A feature owns the UI
and the frontend-specific data access it needs; do not move feature-specific code
into `shared` merely because two components inside the same feature use it.

`shared` suits reusable UI primitives or behavior that genuinely crosses
features — a confirmation dialog, a generic loading indicator, a reusable table
primitive, a formatting pipe — not a dumping ground.

Avoid global service folders containing unrelated feature services, giant
`shared` directories, and choosing Signals or RxJS merely because one is newer
than the other.

canonical_policy.name: Development seeding defaults to representative data
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: For an empty Development database, maintain a small deterministic representative seed dataset covering meaningful states and relationships.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Small representative deterministic dataset, meaningful states and no combinatorial invention covered.

context_quotes:
- By default, maintain a small, deterministic, representative seed dataset for
  an empty Development database, covering the main meaningful states and
  relationships needed to exercise the application.
- Development seeding is an Infrastructure/bootstrap concern: it may use

Cover the main meaningful states and relationships, for example where
applicable: newly created; active or in progress; completed; inactive or
archived; entities with and without optional values; with and without optional
relationships; representative status values; meaningful boundary states. Do not
attempt every combination. When the required entity graph or scenarios are
complex, the task requirements should describe the dataset explicitly rather
than leaving Claude to invent a large generic object graph.

| Scenario | Default technique |
|---|---|
| Read-only entity query | `AsNoTracking()` when useful |
| Read model | Database-side projection |
| Primary-key entity lookup | `FindAsync` when its semantics fit |
| Complex entity graph | Explicit `Include` / projection |
| Set-based mass update/delete | `ExecuteUpdateAsync` / `ExecuteDeleteAsync` when appropriate |
| Normal query | Ordinary LINQ |
| Measured extremely hot query | Consider a compiled query |
| Multiple commits requiring atomicity | Explicit transaction |
| Production schema change | Reviewed migration script, controlled deployment |
| Empty Development database | Run the maintained development seeder |
| Need a fresh local seed dataset | Recreate the local database explicitly |
